fields.title: Out-of-product communication: what they say about you when you are not in the room
fields.keyTakeaway: External communication works cumulatively, not like a campaign: one message repeated by everyone and confirmed by third parties. Measuring it in leads is pointless: it changes what the client brings to the table.
fields.checkQuestion: A publication in an industry trade journal generated zero leads. Does this mean it was useless?
fields.blocks/0/text: The key question of this node: **how to communicate with consumers outside the product?**
fields.blocks/1/items/0: **One message**—what you want people to say about you. One, not five, and repeated by everyone: website, sales, support, publications.
fields.blocks/1/items/1: **Third-party voices**—customers, partners, industry experts. They convince better than any of your own words and cannot be bought directly.
fields.blocks/1/items/2: **Regular presence**—publications, speaking engagements, case breakdowns. Works over years and builds up.
fields.blocks/1/items/3: **Response to bad news**—a pre-arranged procedure: who speaks, how fast, what we admit. An outage, crash, or leak tests communication harder than any launch.
fields.blocks/2/text:
Message: "first invoice in four minutes, with no setup or training."

What was done: a biweekly breakdown of common invoice errors in an industry blog, presentations at two accounting conferences, customer stories with numbers.

Direct leads from this were minimal.

What changed in two years: in 41% of deals, the customer came in already knowing who we are (up from 9%); the sales cycle shrank by a third; the argument "who are you anyway" disappeared from sales conversations.

Measured not by leads, but by the share of clients who knew about us before the first contact.
fields.blocks/2/title: Reestr, two years of building momentum
fields.blocks/3/text: When the service is down for four hours, there is no time to coordinate. Decide in advance: who writes, where, after how many minutes, what exactly we admit, and what we promise. Silence in such hours costs more than the outage itself.
fields.blocks/3/title: Crisis communication cannot be invented in the middle of a crisis
fields.blocks/4/text: External communication does not replace a product and does not accelerate sales in the current quarter. It changes the background against which all other efforts take place—and that is why it is evaluated over a one-year horizon, not a monthly one.
